big: The Union Budget is not just a speech. It is a spending plan of about ₹53.5 lakh crore. Where that money goes decides which sectors get orders, and which stocks follow.

lines: Why do capital goods stocks react to the Budget?
Government capex on roads, railways and defence becomes orders for companies. Defence alone takes about 14.7% of central spending. That spending can also crowd in private investment.

small: ₹ lakh crore, as in the lesson
alt: Bars of total spending and defence spending
caps: Total spending is about ₹53.5 lakh crore.
That is roughly 14.7% of the total.

q: Government capex on roads and rail mainly helps whom?
opts: Only the banks lending to retail
Only the foreign tourists in cities
Only the firms that pay no tax
why: Banks gain indirectly, not mainly. It does not answer what was asked.
Tourism is not the main channel. The details here point elsewhere.
Tax status has no link to orders. That does not match this case.
Capex turns into orders for builders and suppliers.

q: What does 'crowding in' mean for capex?
opts: Public spending blocks all private firms
Public spending can draw private investment
Private firms leave the market fully
why: That describes crowding out, the opposite. That does not match this case.
Public projects can encourage private investment too.
Capex means projects are going ahead. It does not fit the facts given.
It does not push private firms out. It does not answer what was asked.

q: Defence takes about what share of central spending, per the lesson?
why: 1.5% is far too low for the figure.
47% is far too high for the figure.
90% would leave little for anything else.

q: A client asks whether to buy defence stocks 'because of the Budget'. What is sound?
opts: Say the Budget guarantees a rise
Tell her to buy before the news
Avoid explaining and just sell it
why: A Budget cannot guarantee a price. It does not answer what was asked.
Buying on a hint is a tip. It does not answer what was asked.
Link and suitability keep advice honest. This fits the facts given.
Selling without explaining helps nobody. That does not match this case.

pts: Budget spending turns into orders for capex-linked sectors.
Defence is about 14.7% of central spending, per the lesson.
Explain the link. Never promise a result.
